name: Can feasibility assessments be used for remodels, not just new builds?

mainEntity.name: Do homeowners need a construction feasibility assessment for major remodels and additions?
mainEntity.text: Do homeowners need a construction feasibility assessment for major remodels and additions?

acceptedAnswer.text: Feasibility assessments are not only for new homes. Major remodels and additions can run into structure, foundation, access, and code issues that make the original plan unrealistic. In older Los Angeles-area homes, adding square footage may trigger structural upgrades, fire-life-safety changes, or other requirements that materially change the budget. A good assessment can help decide whether a project should stay a remodel, become an addition, or shift to a rebuild strategy. It should also identify how much of the existing house can stay in place without creating construction inefficiency. This is especially valuable when the owner wants to preserve architectural character but also wants modern living space. A proper assessment helps avoid getting halfway into design before discovering the concept is too disruptive or too costly.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Major remodels and additions can still face feasibility issues with structure, access, staging, code upgrades, and permit triggers. An assessment helps determine whether the project should be a remodel, addition, partial rebuild, or full teardown instead.
